newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open flat to $5 a tonne lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open flat to $5 a tonne lower.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open unchanged to $5 per tonne lower on Monday, in line with losses overnight in London, traders said.

London cocoa futures drifted lower in sluggish trading early Monday, but the benchmark September contract continued to hold above key chart support at 1,000 stg. At the midday break, September was down 10 stg, at 1,008 stg, after ranging narrowly from 1,013 to 1,005 stg. December fell seven stg, to 1,045 stg.

On Friday, New York cocoa futures ended firmer, but well off the day's peaks. September rose $4 per tonne, to $1,517, after ranging between $1,537 and $1,515. Second-month December also closed $4 firmer, at $1,564, while the rest ended up $3.
On the charts, traders pegged support at $1,513-$1,510 and then $1,500. On the upside, nearby resistance was seen at $1,540, followed by $1,547-$1,550 and a gap between $1,561 and $1,570.

The latest CFTC Commitment of Traders report released late Friday showed a decrease in the speculative (non-commercials and nonreportable) net long position to 19,443 lots as of July 29. The data was in line with expectations, traders said.

The CFTC Commitment of Traders report showed non-commercial long positions decreased by 3,112 lots in the two weeks ended July 29, to 19,399 lots. Non-commercial short positions increased by 452 lots, to 4,019 lots.
Commercial long positions in the two weeks rose by 1,307 lots, to 63,379 lots and commercial short positions fell by 3,531 lots, to 82,822 lots.
Nonreportable long positions decreased by 478 lots, to 15,040 lots, while nonreportable short positions increased by 796 lots, to 10,977 lots.
